newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle lower in technical selloff.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle lower in technical selloff.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled down sharply for the second straight session in technically driven trade ahead of USDA's Florida crop estimate, dealers said.
Follow-through selling from the previous negative close and the 6,936 puts assigned following Friday's March options expiry fueled the day's losses, analysts said.
They pegged nearby technical support at 78.00 cents a lb in March delivery, and at 82.00 cents in May.
Most-active March ended down 2.30 cents at 80.90 cents, traded 82.85 to 80.50 cents. The back months settled 2.60 to 2.10 cents lower in volume estimated at 6,000 lots.
Meanwhile, players awaited the USDA forecast, slated for release before the market opens Wednesday. The estimate is the first official tally of the crop since the Jan 19 freeze.

Analysts expect USDA to put the crop between 205 million and 210 million 90-lb boxes, with yields at 1.50 gallons per box. Previously, the crop was seen at a record 220 boxes with yields at 1.50 gallons per box.
Also undermining the market were forecasts for warm weather across the Florida citrus belt for the next 10 days. Earlier forecasts cited the possibility of another freeze.
"During the next 10 days there is little if any threat of frost/freeze damage in the citrus belt of central and southern Florida," Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis, said.
